name: Six Flags Magic Mountain
tagline: The self-declared coaster capital of the world, and for once the marketing is close to true.
summary: Six Flags Magic Mountain in Valencia holds more roller coasters than any other park on this site, stacked on a hillside an hour north of Los Angeles. It is a coaster park first and a theme park second, and the crowds are Disneyland-sized on summer Saturdays.
intro: Magic Mountain opened in 1971 as a family park and spent the next five decades building a broad coaster lineup. This guide currently tracks ten current coaster records, plus historical pages for retired X2 and permanently closed Superman: Escape from Krypton. That is the guide’s coverage, not a claim to the park’s complete operating coaster count; check current park operations before planning a visit.

The park is built on a hill, but official land labels matter when planning it: Ninja is in Samurai Summit, Tatsu is in Rapids Camp Crossing, Twisted Colossus is in Screampunk District and Goliath is in Goliath Plaza. Use the current official park map for walking routes rather than assuming those rides share a land.

Magic Mountain’s current all-day paid queue products are Fast Lane Reserve and Fast Lane Ultimate. They apply to participating rides under the selected date’s rules and availability. Check the operating calendar, current price and the party’s ride priorities before deciding whether a product adds value.

lands.name: Six Flags Plaza
lands.summary: The entrance plaza, home to Full Throttle’s launches and 160-foot loop.
description: Six Flags Plaza is Full Throttle’s official location. Six Flags describes a 70-mph launch, a 160-foot loop and a backwards launch out of the tunnel.
Beyond Full Throttle the plaza holds the park’s main guest services, lockers and the tram drop from the parking lot. Gold Rusher’s official location is METROPOLIS, so plan its stop separately.
lands.vibe: Entry-plaza energy, with Full Throttle’s launches and loop.
highlights: Full Throttle’s 160-foot loop in Six Flags Plaza
tips: Check Full Throttle’s current queue when passing through Six Flags Plaza; its minimum is 54 inches and other restrictions still apply.
Buy lockers here, not at individual rides: several coasters require loose articles in a paid locker and the plaza lockers are the cheapest per-hour.

lands.name: DC Universe
lands.summary: Batman: The Ride’s official land, separate from Riddler’s Revenge in METROPOLIS.
description: Six Flags places Batman: The Ride in DC UNIVERSE. The compact inverted coaster combines loops, rolls and turns in suspended seating.
The Riddler’s Revenge belongs to METROPOLIS, so use the official map to plan those as separate land stops rather than a single DC UNIVERSE cluster.
lands.vibe: Concrete and capes: high-intensity coasters with comic paint jobs and no shade to speak of.
highlights: Batman: The Ride, the West Coast invert
tips: Choose a DC UNIVERSE stop using the day’s current queue and conditions; no particular hour guarantees a short line.
Check Batman’s restrictions and restraint fit with attraction staff before boarding.

lands.name: Samurai Summit
lands.summary: Ninja’s official land, with a preserved historical page for permanently closed Superman.
description: Six Flags places Ninja in Samurai Summit. The suspended coaster swings through the hillside’s trees and requires a 42-inch minimum plus separate physical requirements.
Superman: Escape from Krypton’s legacy listing also names Samurai Summit, but that ride is permanently closed. Tatsu’s official location is Rapids Camp Crossing; it is not assigned to this land.
lands.vibe: Hillside terrain and Ninja’s swinging suspended trains.
tips: Use the official park map and Guest Relations guidance to plan access to Samurai Summit.
Ninja is the summit's 42-inch ride and the one younger-sibling ride worth the climb.

lands.name: Cyclone Bay (legacy guide label)
lands.summary: A previous guide label retained as a historical reference, not a current ride or dining assignment.
description: Earlier versions of this guide assigned rides and food to Cyclone Bay. Those records now use separately verified current locations; this page retains the old guide URL as a historical reference.
Use current official labels for ride planning: Twisted Colossus is in Screampunk District, Goliath is in Goliath Plaza and West Coast Racers is in The Underground.
lands.vibe: Historical guide label; use verified current attraction locations.
highlights: Use the current official map and verified land labels
tips: Check the current official map before using an older area name for navigation.
No current ride or food record in this guide is assigned to Cyclone Bay.

lands.name: Baja Ridge
lands.summary: The eastern ridge line, home to Viper's three loops and the park's steepest drop on Goliath's far side approach.
description: Baja Ridge is the stretch of park between the plaza loop and the back bay, and its landmark is Viper's interlocking corkscrews, visible from the parking lot and responsible for a meaningful share of the park's souvenir neck pillows. It is a 1990 Arrow multilooper in full voice.

The ridge also catches the afternoon sun later than the summit does, which makes it a decent late-day zone. Viper at sunset, with the valley going orange behind the loops, is one of the park's signature moments.
lands.vibe: Sun-baked ridge with classic loop-pile silhouettes and the smell of funnel cake drifting up from the plaza.
tips: Viper's shoulder harnesses are famously unforgiving on wide shoulders — keep your head back against the headrest through the loops.
Save this strip for late afternoon when the summit crowd drains downhill.

lands.name: Rapids Camp Crossing
lands.summary: Tatsu’s official land, combining a major flying coaster with the guide’s existing water-area coverage.
description: Six Flags places Tatsu in Rapids Camp Crossing. Its flying ride position and pretzel loop make this a major thrill stop; the listed minimum is 54 inches.

This guide also records Katy’s Kettle in Rapids Camp Crossing. Check the current dining directory and attraction-specific restrictions rather than treating the whole area as a lower-height family tier.
lands.vibe: Trees, water noise and strollers: the low-key corner where the park breathes.
tips: Check the water rides’ current operation, queue and weather before planning a cooling break; drying time depends on conditions.
This is the meet-up zone for split parties: central, shaded, and visible.

lands.name: METROPOLIS
lands.summary: The official land for Gold Rusher and The Riddler’s Revenge.
description: Six Flags places Gold Rusher and The Riddler’s Revenge in METROPOLIS. Gold Rusher requires 48 inches; The Riddler’s Revenge requires 54 inches, and both have other ride restrictions.
Official Gold Rusher location and minimum-height reference: https://www.sixflags.com/magicmountain/attractions/gold-rusher.
lands.vibe: A stop for the park’s original mine-train coaster.
highlights: The Riddler’s Revenge, the stand-up coaster
tips: Use the 48-inch minimum when planning Gold Rusher; ask attraction staff about all other restrictions.

lands.name: The Underground
lands.summary: West Coast Racers’ official land, with launched racing and four inversions.
description: Six Flags places West Coast Racers in The Underground. It requires a 54-inch minimum and includes three zero-G rolls and one zero-G stall; plan for launches and inversions.
Official West Coast Racers location, minimum-height and inversion reference: https://www.sixflags.com/magicmountain/attractions/west-coast-racers.
highlights: West Coast Racers’ four inversions and racing launches
tips: West Coast Racers is not an inversion-free beginner or motion-sensitive alternative.

lands.name: Screampunk District
description: Six Flags places Twisted Colossus in Screampunk District. The hybrid coaster uses the former Colossus structure for its racing and inversion layout.
Use Screampunk District on the current official park map rather than the older Cyclone Bay label when planning this stop.
lands.vibe: Hybrid-coaster track and the former Colossus structure.
tips: Check current operations and all posted restrictions before riding.

lands.name: Goliath Plaza
description: Six Flags places Goliath in Goliath Plaza. The large non-inverting coaster combines a major drop, tunnel and sustained helix.
Use Goliath Plaza on the current official park map rather than treating Goliath as part of Cyclone Bay.
tips: Check the current queue and all posted restrictions before riding.

intro: Magic Mountain rewards a plan more than any other park in Southern California, because the hill punishes improvisation. The park's shape is a loop around a mountain with the marquee coasters at the far ends of it, and the mistake every first-timer makes is ping-ponging.

The plan: choose current ride priorities, use their official land assignments to plan a walking route, and check the day’s operations. Tatsu is in Rapids Camp Crossing; Ninja is a separate Samurai Summit stop.

beforeYouGo.title: Compare the date and current Fast Lane offer
beforeYouGo.body: Check the operating calendar, current Fast Lane Reserve/Ultimate terms and selected-date price before buying. A quieter date may reduce the need, but a weekday does not guarantee short waits or make every product poor value.

beforeYouGo.title: Measure everyone before you leave
beforeYouGo.body: The current coasters this guide tracks require 42, 48 or 54 inches. A 46-inch child can meet Ninja’s 42-inch minimum, but cannot meet Gold Rusher’s or Twisted Colossus’s 48-inch minimum. Check all other restrictions too; attraction staff make the final eligibility determination.

beforeYouGo.title: Lockers are per-ride here
beforeYouGo.body: Several coasters require loose articles in lockers at the ride entrance. Bring minimal pockets, and expect the plaza lockers to be the best per-hour deal if you must carry things.

beforeYouGo.title: Check the calendar for daily operation
beforeYouGo.body: Magic Mountain runs reduced schedules much of the year, with some weekdays dark entirely outside summer and holidays. Verify your exact date before booking anything non-refundable.

morningPlan.body: Aim to arrive before the posted opening with time for parking, security and entry. The time needed varies by date and arrival conditions.
Prioritize Tatsu in Rapids Camp Crossing if it is operating and suitable for your party. Use the current official map for the route.
After Tatsu, continue to the next suitable current ride. Ninja is a separate stop in Samurai Summit, subject to its 42-inch minimum and physical restrictions.
Plan Batman: The Ride in DC UNIVERSE and The Riddler’s Revenge in METROPOLIS as separate land stops.

middayPlan.body: Plan a meal break around the party’s needs and the current food-service queues. An early or later meal can be an option, but no restaurant-emptying time is guaranteed.

Twisted Colossus is in Screampunk District, Goliath is in Goliath Plaza and West Coast Racers is in The Underground. Choose the next stop using current queues, the map and the party’s full ride restrictions.
Water rides at the crossing while the heat peaks, then Viper on the ridge as the sun drops.

eveningPlan.body: Consider a repeat ride if it is operating and the current queue fits the remaining time; late-day waits can change.
Consider Full Throttle in Six Flags Plaza if it is operating and its queue fits the remaining time. Check the actual closing time and your last transportation connection.

rookieMistakes: Repeatedly crossing the hill without a route plan. Use the current official map to reduce backtracking; the time saved varies by route and party.
Buying Fast Lane without checking the selected date, participating ride list, availability and current product terms.
Planning a current ride on X2 or Superman: Escape from Krypton. Both are permanently closed; their preserved pages are historical.
Assuming the park closes at six. Check the hours; summer and fall haunt dates run later.
Treating Gold Rusher’s gentler profile as permission for a short rider — its official minimum is 48 inches.
ifYouOnlyHaveOneDay: Consider Tatsu in Rapids Camp Crossing early if it is operating and suitable for your party.
Plan Ninja as a separate Samurai Summit stop; its 42-inch minimum does not replace physical restrictions.
Batman in DC UNIVERSE and Riddler’s Revenge in METROPOLIS for suitable riders.
Twisted Colossus in Screampunk District and Goliath in Goliath Plaza.
West Coast Racers in The Underground for riders meeting its 54-inch minimum and other restrictions.
Gold Rusher in METROPOLIS for riders meeting its 48-inch minimum and other restrictions.
Viper at sunset, Full Throttle at close, subject to the day’s operations.

intro: The official accessibility page encourages guests seeking reasonable accommodations to obtain the IBCCES Accessibility Card (IAC); it does not establish mandatory advance registration. Only IBCCES issues that card. Guests present it at the Ride Information Center on arrival, discuss their accommodation needs and the applicable physical criteria, and receive program details from staff. The program does not provide immediate boarding.

Ride access and physical eligibility are separate questions. Current posted rules and attraction staff’s determination still apply; a card, height match or an observer’s impression does not certify permission to ride. See the [official accessibility page](https://www.sixflags.com/magicmountain/accessibility) and its [linked Guest Accessibility Guide](https://media.qrtiger.com/files/2025/07/gag_sfmm-hhla.pdf), version 25-1.0.0. Confirm current arrangements with Guest Relations or the Ride Information Center.

The linked guide describes Magic Mover as a hillside rail cable car with ramp access for mobility devices. Check its current operation and access points with staff rather than assuming a special summit route or access to every ride loading area.

strollerRental.priceNote: Official FAQ lists first-come, first-served rentals; confirm current stock, options, deposit and pricing. Source: https://www.sixflags.com/magicmountain/frequently-asked-questions

companionRestrooms: The linked guide directs guests to the park map, Team Members or Guest Relations for companion-restroom locations. Confirm the location and access needed during your visit.

quietSpaces.name: Sensory-break location check
quietSpaces.where: Ask Guest Relations or the Ride Information Center
quietSpaces.note: Specific quiet-room locations and access arrangements were not established by this review. Ask staff for a suitable break location and current conditions; do not assume an outdoor shaded area or First Aid is a designated sensory space.

serviceAnimalRelief: The current official accessibility page identifies an inside relief area near the entrance to Samurai Summit, between Gold Rusher and Jet Stream, and an outside area at Guest Drop-Off. Confirm the current locations with staff.
sensoryNotes: The linked guide describes Full Throttle’s audio, fog, lighting and strobe effects, and West Coast Racers’ audio and lighting. West Coast Racers also has four inversions. Check those elements against the rider’s needs.
Tatsu’s flying position and hillside layout can create height exposure; its official land is Rapids Camp Crossing.
The fall haunt overlay adds sudden scares along the midways after dark in season.
mobilityNotes: Use the current official park map and staff advice to choose an accessible walking route and check any hillside transport operation; no fixed route duration or special summit service is promised here.

Check the separate transfer and boarding requirements for each current attraction. Staff are not trained to lift or carry guests onto rides; the linked guide says transfers must be accomplished independently or with help from the guest’s party.
The guide describes wheelchair/ECV battery recharging at the Ride Information Center; ask staff about current access and arrangements.
visionHearingNotes: The official accessibility page lists limited Braille and large-print Guest Accessibility Guides at Guest Services, first come, first served.

The linked 2025 Guest Accessibility Guide says assisted listening devices are available upon request and directs guests to Guest Relations. It does not establish availability at a specific attraction; confirm the device and intended use with staff.

The current official accessibility page says ASL interpretation for live shows can be requested at least one week in advance through its request form. Check the current procedure and show choices with Guest Services: https://www.sixflags.com/magicmountain/accessibility

tips.title: Check queues before deciding on Fast Lane
tips.body: The value of Fast Lane Reserve or Ultimate depends on the visit date, available rides, current queues and your priorities. Read the official selected-date offer rather than treating all weekdays or weekends as the same.

tips.title: Two cars on the mountain beat one
tips.body: For mixed thrill tolerance, choose a reunion point on the official map before splitting up. Tatsu is in Rapids Camp Crossing and Ninja is in Samurai Summit; do not assign all thrill riders to one summit cluster.

tips.title: Check retirement status before planning
tips.body: X2 is permanently retired and Superman: Escape from Krypton is permanently closed. The preserved attraction pages are historical and do not establish current ride availability.

tips.title: Check the current drink offer
tips.body: Compare the current drink-product price, refill rules, included beverages and your party’s expected use before buying. Heat or a second walking loop alone does not establish savings.

tips.title: Check the parking route on arrival
tips.body: Walking distance depends on the assigned parking area, party and conditions. Ask staff about the current pedestrian route, accessible drop-off and any operating parking transport rather than assuming a fixed walk or tram-time saving.

tips.title: the fall haunt changes the park
tips.body: After dark on haunt nights, several midways become scare zones and some family areas close. If you are visiting in late September or October with young kids, check which nights run the overlay.

faqs.q: How many roller coasters does Magic Mountain have?
faqs.a: This guide tracks ten current coaster records at Magic Mountain and keeps X2 and Superman: Escape from Krypton as historical pages. That is the site’s coverage, not the park’s complete operating coaster count. Check Six Flags’ current attraction list and daily operations for a park-wide count.

faqs.q: Can you do Magic Mountain in one day?
faqs.a: A single day can cover your current priorities if the operations, queues and walking route fit. Use the official land assignments and park map to reduce backtracking, then decide whether more time or a line-skip product suits the date.

faqs.q: What is the height requirement situation at Magic Mountain?
faqs.a: Among the current coasters this guide tracks, Ninja requires 42 inches; Gold Rusher, Goliath and Twisted Colossus require 48; West Coast Racers, Tatsu, Full Throttle, Viper, Batman and Riddler’s Revenge require 54. Gold Rusher is not an under-48-inch option. Height alone does not establish permission to ride; all other restrictions apply and attraction staff decide final eligibility.

faqs.q: Is Fast Lane worth it at Magic Mountain?
faqs.a: Compare Fast Lane Reserve and Fast Lane Ultimate for your selected date and priorities. Reserve uses a virtual wait with a return time; Ultimate allows an immediate Fast Lane entrance reservation, not immediate boarding. Both limit you to one reservation at a time and participating rides subject to availability. Admission is separate, and [Fright Fest](/events/fright-fest-magic-mountain/) haunted attractions require their own pass; no fixed number of additional rides is guaranteed. Official terms: https://www.sixflags.com/magicmountain/fast-lane.

faqs.q: How do I get to Magic Mountain without a car?
faqs.a: From Los Angeles Union Station, take Metrolink’s Antelope Valley Line to Newhall, then a Santa Clarita Transit connection to McBean Regional Transit Center and route 3 or 7 to Six Flags. Check current timetables for every leg and the last return connections before choosing transit for a [Fright Fest](/events/fright-fest-magic-mountain/) night; service after an 11 p.m. park exit is not guaranteed.

faqs.q: What should I ride first at rope drop?
faqs.a: Tatsu in Rapids Camp Crossing is a strong early option if it is operating and your party meets all restrictions. Plan Ninja separately in Samurai Summit and use the current map for the remaining land stops.

faqs.q: Does Magic Mountain have good food?
faqs.a: This guide records limited dining coverage rather than a complete park-wide tasting assessment. Check the current official dining directory, menu, price, opening status and dietary information before choosing a meal.

faqs.q: Does a height wristband guarantee admission at later rides?
faqs.a: Do not assume a measurement or wristband prevents later remeasurement. Ask Guest Relations about current measurement and wristband procedures, and follow each attraction’s posted restrictions. Attraction staff make the final eligibility determination. Source: https://www.sixflags.com/magicmountain/frequently-asked-questions

faqs.q: Can we rely on transit after a late-night event?
faqs.a: Check the dated return timetables before visiting: route 3 or 7 from Six Flags, the connection from McBean Regional Transit Center to Newhall, and the last Antelope Valley Line train toward Los Angeles. Do not assume the full trip is available after 11 p.m.; plan an earlier departure or arrange alternative transportation if the last connections do not fit.

gettingThere.parking: Follow staff directions for the assigned parking area, pedestrian route and accessible drop-off. Walking time and any parking-transport operation vary; no fixed walk or tram saving is established by this guide.
transportation: By car: use current navigation and traffic conditions for the route to Magic Mountain Parkway. Driving time from Los Angeles varies by starting point, traffic and road conditions.

By transit from Los Angeles Union Station: Metrolink Antelope Valley Line to Newhall, then Santa Clarita Transit to McBean Regional Transit Center (MRTC), then route 3 or 7 to Six Flags. The city’s official guide lists routes 5/6, 4/14 or 12 for the Newhall–MRTC connection; use current schedules to choose the departure.
By rideshare: well-served, with a designated drop-off lane at the main gate.

Before a [Fright Fest](/events/fright-fest-magic-mountain/) visit, check the final return departure on each leg, including the last train from Newhall. A complete transit trip after an 11 p.m. park exit is not guaranteed; arrange an earlier exit or alternative transportation when needed.

Current [Santa Clarita Transit bus timetables](https://santaclaritatransit.com/routes-schedules/) and [Metrolink train timetables](https://metrolinktrains.com/schedules/). Official route references: [Santa Clarita Transit](https://santaclaritatransit.com/services/getting-to-six-flags-magic-mountain/) and [Metrolink](https://metrolinktrains.com/explore/los-angeles-county/six-flags-magic-mountain/).
gettingThere.entranceNote: Allow time for parking, security and park entry before the posted opening; check current arrival instructions rather than relying on a fixed processing time.
